title: The host cannot read a specific control grant's state, so an ambiguous begin refusal stays unresolvable
outcome: A host can ask Engram, read-only, for the state of one exact grant of its own session (issued, begun, completed, expired, superseded, or not found), with begun evidence where it exists. A begin-unknown reconcile can then resolve the cases a typed refusal leaves ambiguous (grant_scope_mismatch, unknown_control_schema) without guessing, re-evaluating blindly or needing an operator's database read.
acceptance: A new host-control read takes the session's routing token plus a grant id and returns that grant's current state and begun_at/completed_at evidence. A grant not found is reported distinctly from never-begun. A grant belonging to another session is refused. The read mutates nothing; unlike session_status it does not lazily expire grants.
The addition is additive on the host wire: no existing request or response changes shape. The behavioral-control-plane doc lists it under shipped host channel operations.
Tests cover each state, not found, another session's grant, and that the read changes no row.

completion.summary: Delivered additive host-only turn_grant_read with exact same-session historical grant state/timestamps, distinct not_found and foreign-session refusal, one credential-and-grant snapshot, no writes or lazy expiry. Nine-stage full gate, complete verified Codex/Claude round3, all four live stores ready and fresh independent acceptance 3/3. Committed, installed with backup and pushed fast-forward. Low follow-ups w-929d05e48ae1 and w-c2ef96adc0d3 retained independently.
